title: They Lost 4-2 to Japan. Three Days Later, India's U18 Boys Beat Korea 4-1. The Semi-Final Is On.
excerpt: Captain Ketan Kushwaha scored twice as India bounced back in the U18 Asia Cup in Kakamigahara, levelling with Korea and Japan on six points in Pool A.
body:
Three days after a bruising 4-2 defeat to hosts Japan, India's U18 men's hockey team produced one of their most complete performances of the tournament — dismantling Korea 4-1 in their third Pool A match of the U18 Asia Cup 2026 in Kakamigahara, Japan.

Captain Ketan Kushwaha was the standout, scoring twice from penalty corner rebounds, while Varinder Singh and Shahrukh Ali added a goal each. Korean captain Yun Jaehyeok's solitary penalty corner conversion was the only blemish on what was otherwise a dominant Indian display.

## Two Goals in Five Minutes Set the Tone

India came out with unmistakable intent. In the third minute, Rahul Yadav played an incisive pass to Kushwaha from a penalty corner. The Korean goalkeeper saved his initial shot, but the Indian skipper was alive to the rebound, slotting it into the net for 1-0.

Two minutes later, the lead had doubled. Gazee Khan showed excellent vision to pick out Varinder Singh unmarked near the goal, and the forward finished with the composure of a player twice his age. At 2-0 inside five minutes, India had already avenged the hesitant start that had cost them against Japan.

Korea pulled one back in the 21st minute when captain Yun Jaehyeok converted a penalty corner, but India's defensive composure — absent in the Japan match — held firm through the rest of the second quarter.

## Kushwaha's Second Killed the Contest

The third quarter began as the first had — with India on the front foot. Another penalty corner in the 36th minute, another rebound that the Korean defence failed to clear, and another Kushwaha finish. At 3-1, the result was effectively settled.

Korea came agonisingly close in the 53rd minute when Kim Doyun's deflection beat the defence, but goalkeeper Ayush Rajak produced a sharp stick save that preserved India's two-goal cushion. Within sixty seconds of that save, Shahrukh Ali scored India's fourth — a powerful strike in the 54th minute that sealed what had been a statement performance.

## What It Means for the Semi-Final Race

The victory lifts India to six points, level with Korea and Japan in Pool A. With their final group match against Chinese Taipei on June 3, India are well-placed to secure a top-two finish and a semi-final berth.

The turnaround from the Japan loss is significant. India had conceded early and chased the game in that 4-2 defeat. Against Korea, the script was flipped entirely — two goals inside five minutes, controlled aggression through the middle quarters, and clinical finishing when the chances came.

## The Women Are Doing Their Part Too

While the men bounced back, India's U18 women's team has been flawless. They have won both their Pool A matches — beating Malaysia in the opener and then defeating Korea 3-1 on May 31, with Nousheen Naz continuing her remarkable tournament form (she has scored in every game). The women face Singapore on June 2 and are already favourites to top their pool.

## For the Diaspora

For the Indian hockey community abroad — from the weekend turf leagues in the UK to the growing pickup scene in the American Midwest — these junior tournaments matter more than the scorelines suggest. They are the pipeline. Kushwaha, Varinder, Nousheen, Shruti — these are the names that will populate the senior squads for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and beyond. The U18 Asia Cup is where the audition begins.

India's men play Chinese Taipei on June 3 at 1:30 PM IST. The women face Singapore on June 2. The semi-finals are on June 5.
author: Diaspora Desk
